title: regional-saturation-traceback-datapull-2026-12-19
summary: Dataset extract for a regional capacity incident that caused cross-region spillover: telemetry for saturation, queueing, and throttle events across GPU types during 2026-12-12 00:00 -> 2026-12-13 12:00 UTC. Purpose: provide tables and raw queries for postmortem and action items for autoscaler and routing fixes.
sql_queries:
-- queue depth by region/gpu_type
SELECT region, gpu_type, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY queue_depth) AS q95, max(gpu_util_pct) AS peak_util, sum(throttle_events) AS throttle_count FROM gpu_telemetry WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-12-12T00:00:00Z' AND '2026-12-13T12:00:00Z' GROUP BY region, gpu_type;

-- throttle event detail (first 100 rows)
SELECT ts, region, gpu_id, request_id, throttle_reason, queued_ms, model_variant FROM throttle_events WHERE ts >= '2026-12-12T00:00:00Z' ORDER BY ts LIMIT 100;

-- KV cache miss spike correlation with long-context requests
SELECT hour(ts) AS hr, sum(case when context_tokens > 8192 then 1 else 0 end) AS long_ctx_requests, avg(kv_cache_miss_rate) AS avg_miss FROM request_telemetry WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-12-12' AND '2026-12-13' GROUP BY hr ORDER BY hr;

-- autoscaler scale up lag (time between queue crossing threshold and new node readiness)
SELECT event_time, region, gpu_pool, queue_depth, scale_action, timestamp_diff('second', queue_cross_ts, node_ready_ts) AS scale_lag_secs FROM autoscaler_audit WHERE date(ts) = '2026-12-12' ORDER BY scale_lag_secs DESC LIMIT 50;
findings: Spike in queued work (95p queue depth > 15) in us-west1 and asia-east1 coincided with batch ingestion jobs from customer X and an internal nightly backup starting at 2026-12-12T05:45Z.

Autoscaler did not trigger fast enough: multiple pools showed scale_lag_secs > 180s for the first 6 scale events in us-west1; root cause traced to cooldown setting + kube API throttling during the window.
Throttles were dominated by 'QUEUE_FULL' reasons; ~60% of throttle events targeted older quantized model variants which have lower throughput per-GPU and higher memory pressure.

Long-context requests (context_tokens > 8192) generated a KV cache miss spike and increased per-request latency, lowering effective throughput and contributing to saturation on H100 pools serving large-batch-rerank workloads.
Cross-region spillover: routing fallback rules moved requests from us-west1 to us-central1 temporarily, increasing latency and causing localized pressure there as well.
Alerting gaps: the existing 'gpu-util > 85% for 5m' alert fired late; a leading indicator (95p queue depth and cache-miss rate) would have allowed earlier mitigation.
Configuration drift: one production pool in asia-east1 had a nonstandard max_burst_size override that bypassed burst capacity, reducing available headroom during spikes.
recommendations: Reduce autoscaler cooldown for critical pools from 300s -> 90s and add immediate preemptive scale policy when 95p queue depth > 10.
Introduce model-variant throughput profiles into routing so that high-memory, low-throughput variants are deprioritized during region pressure.
Add a new early-warning alert: 95p queue depth > 8 AND kv_cache_miss_rate increase > 30% over 10m => page ops-team and trigger emergency-burst-policy.
Temporarily block scheduled heavy batch jobs in regions with peak_util > 85% until autoscaler changes are deployed; coordinate with data-team for window rescheduling.
Audit all pools for custom max_burst_size overrides and revert any nonstandard settings to the baseline policy unless approved by infra-ops.
Instrument request-level tags for large-context workloads and consider routing to dedicated long-context pools with tailored caching strategies.
action_items: (AI-1) infra: implement autoscaler cooldown change and deploy to us-west1 and asia-east1 by 2027-01-10 - assigned to Diego Ramirez - JIRA-INF-3835
(AI-2) routing: add variant throughput metadata to routing decisions - assigned to Priya Nair - PR #2147
(AI-3) ops: create preemptive-alert (95p-queue + kv-miss) and test on staging by 2027-01-07 - assigned to Aisha Patel
(AI-4) data-team: postpone scheduled batch ingestion windows that overlap peak hours in us-west1 until new autoscaler policy is live - coordination note sent
(AI-5) infra: run pool config audit script and rollback nonstandard burst overrides by 2027-01-05 - assigned to Marcus Lee
note: This extract intentionally focuses on telemetry slices that were not fully captured by the initial incident runbook (cache-miss-series and variant-level throttle reasons). Raw logs and full-sized dumps are available in the linked GitHub artifact and S3 bucket referenced from the Confluence page. Use the provided SQL snippets to reproduce the tables in the incident channel.
